result.instructions: Tools for Teamup Calendar, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "What is on the shared team calendar this week, day by day?"; "Find all events mentioning 'inspection' in the next two months."; "Who is signed up for the Saturday workshop?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Teamup Calendar data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run teamup_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run teamup_request_feature to record the request. Pro (unlimited calls, $9/month or $90/year): when the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run teamup_upgrade; it returns a Stripe Checkout link for the user to open. teamup_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: teamup_get_calendar
tools.title: Get calendar
tools.description: The calendar this connection points at: title, timezone and date settings, custom event fields, sub-calendars, the permission of the calendar key in use and the plan's features. Call this first to learn the sub-calendar ids and the timezone. The calendar key itself is never returned. GET /{calendarKey}/configuration.

tools.name: teamup_list_subcalendars
tools.title: List sub-calendars
tools.description: List the sub-calendars (the colored lanes that events belong to, such as people, rooms or resources). A key with admin permission also sees inactive ones. GET /{calendarKey}/subcalendars.

name_contains.description: Only sub-calendars whose name matches this text.

offset.description: Number of results to skip (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

tools.name: teamup_get_subcalendar
tools.title: Get sub-calendar
tools.description: One sub-calendar by id: name, color, overlap rule, active state and which links may use it. GET /{calendarKey}/subcalendars/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_list_access_keys
tools.title: List access keys
tools.description: List the calendar's access keys (sharing links and user accesses) with name, role, active state and per-sub-calendar permission. Needs a key with admin permission. The secret key values are never returned (they are secrets); use the id and name to tell links apart. GET /{calendarKey}/keys.

name_contains.description: Only keys whose link, user or group name matches this text.

offset.description: Number of results to skip (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

tools.name: teamup_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the events in a date range, optionally only on some sub-calendars. Recurring events are expanded: every occurrence in the range is returned with its own id (series id + -rid- + start). Notes come as markdown. Times use the calendar's timezone unless tz is set. GET /{calendarKey}/events.

end_date.description: Last day, inclusive, yyyy-mm-dd (default: start_date). Needs start_date; at most 366 days after it.

tz.description: Timezone for the times in the reply, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Default: the calendar's timezone.

tools.name: teamup_search_events
tools.title: Search events
tools.description: Search events by keyword (2-100 characters) within a date range (default: today only, so always pass the range you mean). Recurring events are expanded. Paged with limit and offset. GET /{calendarKey}/events?query=.

end_date.description: Last day, inclusive, yyyy-mm-dd (default: start_date). Needs start_date; at most 366 days after it.

tz.description: Timezone for the times in the reply, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Default: the calendar's timezone.

offset.description: Number of results to skip (default 0). Pass the previous reply's next_offset.

tools.name: teamup_get_event
tools.title: Get event
tools.description: One event by id: title, times, sub-calendars, location, who, notes (markdown), recurrence rule, custom fields, signups, comments, attachments (metadata), version, change history and reminders. Use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) for one occurrence of a recurring event. GET /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

tools.name: teamup_list_changed_events
tools.title: List changed events
tools.description: Events created, changed or deleted since a Unix timestamp (at most 30 days back), for syncing. A recurring event comes back once, as its series, not as occurrences. Deleted events carry delete_dt. Pass the reply's timestamp as since_timestamp next time so nothing is missed. GET /{calendarKey}/events?modifiedSince=.

since_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, at most 30 days in the past.

mode.description: synchronize (default): events created and deleted after the timestamp are left out. monitor: they are returned too.

tools.name: teamup_list_event_signups
tools.title: List event signups
tools.description: The people signed up for an event (name, email, id). Signups must be enabled on the event. GET /{calendarKey}/events/{id}/signups.

tools.name: teamup_create_event
tools.title: Create event
tools.description: WRITE: create an event. Needs a calendar key with add or modify permission. Give at least subcalendar_ids, start and end. Not idempotent: a repeated call creates a second event. The reply holds the new event and an undo_id; teamup_undo_event_action removes the event again within one hour. POST /{calendarKey}/events.

subcalendar_ids.description: Sub-calendar ids the event belongs to (from teamup_list_subcalendars).

start.description: Start, e.g. 2026-10-14T09:00:00 (calendar timezone) or with an offset such as +02:00. For an all-day event: yyyy-mm-dd.

end.description: End, same format as start. Must not be before start.

all_day.description: True for an all-day event (default false).

rrule.description: Recurrence rule (iCalendar RRULE, e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=10). Omit for a single event.

custom.description: Values of custom fields, keyed by field id (see teamup_get_calendar -> fields).

signup_limit.description: Maximum signups; required by Teamup when signup_enabled is true.

signup_visibility.description: Who sees the signups: all_users or users_with_modify_permission.

comments_visibility.description: Who sees the comments: all_users or users_with_modify_permission.

tools.name: teamup_update_event
tools.title: Update event
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an event; fields you leave out keep their value (the event is read first and sent back with its version, so a concurrent edit is refused instead of overwritten; an event without a version is not changed). Needs modify permission. For a recurring event pass redit; use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) with single or future. Attachments are not touched. The reply holds the event and an undo_id for one hour (teamup_undo_event_action). PUT /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

event_id.description: Event id (occurrence id for one occurrence of a recurring event).

redit.description: Which occurrences of a recurring event: single (only this one), future (this and all later ones) or all.

subcalendar_ids.description: Sub-calendar ids the event belongs to (from teamup_list_subcalendars).

start.description: New start (same formats as in teamup_create_event).

notes.description: New notes, in markdown. Replaces the old notes.

rrule.description: New recurrence rule; with redit all or future only. An empty string removes the recurrence (the series becomes a single event).

custom.description: Custom field values to set, keyed by field id; other custom fields keep their value.

tools.name: teamup_delete_event
tools.title: Delete event
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete an event, or for a recurring event the chosen occurrences. Needs modify permission. Not retried. The reply holds an undo_id; teamup_undo_event_action restores the event within one hour, after that the deletion is permanent. For one occurrence use the occurrence id (123-rid-<unix start>) and redit single (the default); redit all deletes the whole series. DELETE /{calendarKey}/events/{id}.

event_id.description: Event id (occurrence id for one occurrence of a recurring event).

redit.description: For a recurring event: single (default), future or all. With all the whole series is deleted.

version.description: The event's version (from teamup_get_event). If set, the delete is refused when the event changed since.

tools.name: teamup_undo_event_action
tools.title: Undo event change
tools.description: WRITE: undo a recent event creation, update or deletion with the undo_id from that call. Works for one hour only and is refused if someone else changed the event since. PUT /{calendarKey}/events/undo/{undo_id}.

undo_id.description: The undo_id returned by create, update or delete.

tools.name: teamup_create_subcalendar
tools.title: Create sub-calendar
tools.description: WRITE: create a sub-calendar. Needs a calendar key with admin permission, and the plan may limit how many exist. Not idempotent: a repeated call creates a second one. POST /{calendarKey}/subcalendars.

overlap.description: Allow overlapping events on it (default true).

tools.name: teamup_update_subcalendar
tools.title: Update sub-calendar
tools.description: WRITE: change a sub-calendar's name, color, overlap rule or active state; fields you leave out keep their value. Needs admin permission. Making a sub-calendar inactive hides it from users without admin rights. PATCH /{calendarKey}/subcalendars/{id}.

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Teamup Calendar
prompts.description: What you can do with Teamup Calendar here, with example requests to try.
